account.signoutEverywhere.description: Sign yourself out on every computer and browser

account.update.description: Change your own name or email (an email change asks for your password)

activity.summary.description: What MetaRush is doing now: uploads, processing, renders, QA and assistant runs with stages, progress, machines and why anything is waiting

add.cloud.description: Bring files in from a Google Drive or Dropbox folder through your own rclone on this computer, by their IDs (or names, or all of them): each is fetched, checked against the folder's listing and added like the Add box does — footage to the project, pictures to its resources — saying where it came from

add.cloud.list.description: List a Google Drive or Dropbox folder through your own rclone on this computer (each file's ID, name, size, time and checksum), without syncing it; nothing is fetched

add.links.description: Bring in pasted or dropped links: videos (YouTube, TikTok, X, video sites) are imported as footage; GitHub repositories (pinned at a commit) and web pages (dated snapshots) become resources; asks when a link could be either

add.paths.description: Add local files and folders like the Add box: footage to the project (or the Inbox), pictures, SVGs, PDFs and fonts to its resources (or the workspace library), folders as linked folders

add.route.description: Say where files and links would go if added: footage, resources, a linked folder, a link import, a GitHub repository or a web page snapshot

ai.cancel.description: Stop AI work that is waiting or being made

ai.estimate.description: Price AI work — how much a picture, speech, a sound effect, music, a dub or a cloud transcript would cost — and check it may be made (the model and why, up to two alternatives, consent, budget, this computer's key, licence terms); nothing is sent or spent

ai.list.description: List AI work (pictures, voices, sound effects, music, dubs, transcripts, voice copies) with what it cost

ai.local.description: List the AI models that run on this computer — free, no key, nothing leaves it — with whether each is set up and what setting it up downloads

ai.local.setup.description: Set up an AI model that runs on this computer: download its pinned files once, checked by their SHA-256 (people only)

ai.make.description: Make a picture, speech of a script, a sound effect, music, a clip in another voice, a dub or a cloud transcript with an AI service; priced first: needs maxUsd, the agreed estimate, unless your estimates are off

ai.models.description: List the AI services' models for each kind of work — pictures, voices, voice copies, voice change, sound effects, music, dubbing, transcription and video — with dated prices, licence and data terms, and what a project's Content Settings allow

ai.rules.description: Show which AI services a project's work may go to (the AI services part of its Content Settings)

ai.rules.set.description: Change which AI services the work of projects using a project's own Content Settings may go to: none at all, never some providers, or a model chosen for a kind of work (people only: like budgets, a client's rule is a person's decision)

ai.show.description: Show how a piece of AI work was made: the model and why, what was sent, settings, licence and data terms, cost, consent and what it made

ai.voices.description: List the voice copies MetaRush made, whose voice each is and whether it may still be used

ai.voices.copy.description: Copy a person's voice with an AI service, with their consent in force (and, where the service wants it, a recording of them reading its consent script) — people only, priced first

ai.voices.remove.description: Withdraw a voice copy: deleted at the provider, and nothing more is said with it (people only)

asset.archive.description: File clips in the Archive, the one “keep for later” shelf: they leave the Inbox (and, with a project, that project) without going to a project; nothing is deleted

asset.card.description: Show a source's info card: its descriptive name and original file, where it came from, what MetaRush found in it (length, picture and sound, people, words on screen), where it is used and its fixes

asset.delete.description: Delete footage for good — the file, its preview, transcript and speaker data, on every machine — when no project but this one has it and no cut (no version of any cut) uses it; people only

asset.duplicate.description: Resolve a file identical to an existing asset: keep (record its filename as an alias, link to a project; bytes are not stored twice) or skip

asset.fixes.description: Show a source's fixes: its kind, the fixes it is offered, which fit and why (measured), which are ticked, the fixed copy it uses and the cuts that play it

asset.fixes.look.description: Measure a clip again for its fixes (shake, colour, grain, blockiness, voices, loudness, hum, silent ends)

asset.fixes.set.description: Tick or untick a source's fixes (steady, colour, grain, volumes, voices, blocks, loudness, hum, ends, background, edges, larger) or say what kind of source it is; the original is kept and a fixed copy is made on a worker

asset.link.description: Add an existing asset to a project (or remove it with unlink: the footage stays in the workspace, in the Inbox when no project has it)

asset.list.description: List assets in a project, the unassigned inbox, or the whole workspace

asset.move.description: Move footage from one project (or the Inbox) to another; the footage itself doesn't change

asset.names.description: List the better, descriptive names MetaRush suggests for sources (who is in them, what they are about), and which ones “use all” would apply (a name a person gave is never replaced)

asset.names.accept.description: Use MetaRush's better names for sources: all that are waiting, or the ones given; names people gave are kept

asset.precheck.description: Before uploading: find files identical to stored assets (size + first/last-MiB fingerprint), duplicates within the batch, and interrupted uploads that can resume

asset.restore.description: Put clips in the Trash back where they were: their project, collections and the Archive (the Inbox when none is left)

asset.rights.description: Record where a music or audio file comes from and what allows using it

asset.show.description: Show one asset with probe metadata, variants and processing jobs

asset.trash.description: Move clips to the Trash: they disappear from the Inbox, their collections and the Archive (and, with a project, that project) until restored; nothing is deleted until the Trash is emptied. Refused while any project's latest cut uses a clip or another project has it

asset.unarchive.description: Take clips out of the Archive: back in the Inbox unless a project or collection has them

asset.update.description: Rename a clip: its descriptive title (the original filename stays as file info), typed or MetaRush's suggestion; a typed title is never replaced by MetaRush

asset.where.description: List every place footage is used: the projects it is in, projects that see it through a link, and the cuts (and their older versions) that play it

assistant.act.description: Do, answer or set aside what Claude asked for (one card, several at once, or a question card); people only

assistant.apply.description: Apply one of the changes Claude wrote in a conversation, after checking it with the list of proposals

assistant.ask.description: Start a conversation with this machine's Claude Code (it only looks and suggests; people make the changes)

assistant.attach.description: Attach a picture or a PDF to the next message of a conversation (stored by its content; MetaRush asks whether to keep it in the project)

assistant.configure.description: Change a conversation's model, effort or spending limit (from its next message on)

assistant.continue.description: Send a follow-up message (it waits while Claude is working); only on the machine the conversation runs on

assistant.dequeue.description: Remove a waiting message before it is sent

assistant.interrupt.description: Stop what Claude is doing now (the conversation goes on; waiting messages are handed back)

assistant.list.description: List the Claude Code conversations (every machine of the workspace), most recent first

assistant.mode.description: Show whether Claude's changes for you wait for your OK (ask) or run by themselves when they can be undone (auto)

assistant.mode.set.description: Choose whether Claude's changes for you wait for your OK (ask) or run by themselves when they can be undone (auto); people only

assistant.models.description: List the models and effort levels this machine's Claude Code offers (nothing is sent to Claude)

assistant.proposals.description: List the changes and render requests Claude wrote in a conversation, each checked against the latest version of the cut

assistant.settings.description: Show this machine's Claude Code settings (model, effort, limits, how it is billed)

assistant.settings.set.description: Change this machine's Claude Code settings (model, effort, spending limit per conversation, the switch for steps that run by themselves); owners

assistant.show.description: Show one conversation: its messages and what Claude did (with raw, the exact messages and tool output too)

assistant.spending.description: When Auto spends money by itself: with each outside service, whether a person set the project's budget and the team's daily limit (and who); and what Auto spent for you today

assistant.status.description: Check whether Claude Code can run on this machine (version, sign-in, how it is billed, limits); nothing is sent to Claude

assistant.stop.description: Stop the conversation's Claude Code (a later message picks it up again)

assistant.suggestions.description: Suggest a few natural prompts for the current project or workspace

audit.list.description: Read the audit trail (who did what, from which machine)

auth.method.set.description: Choose how people sign in, giving your own sign-in at the same step (owners, on this computer)

auth.reset.description: Put sign-in back to a fresh install's: just the owner on this computer, everyone signed out, people kept with their history (on this computer)

auth.status.description: How people sign in to this MetaRush (just you on this computer, email and password, or Tailscale accounts) and who you are

brand.apply.description: Use the brand in the latest cut — the brand of the Content Settings the project uses (its own, another project's or the default's): its colours, font and logos (a checked change)

brand.set.description: Change the brand of a project's own Content Settings (without a project, the default's — what new projects use): logos (colours are taken from the logo unless a person set them), colours and font; or take what a website snapshot suggests (fromSite) and put it on the project's latest cut (apply, a checked change)

brand.show.description: Show a brand kit — the brand of the Content Settings a project uses (its own, another project's or the default's) or, without a project, the default's — its logos, colours and font, the brand new cuts get, and the project's website snapshots a kit can be suggested from

brand.suggest.description: Suggest a brand kit from a website snapshot: its logo, four colours (primary, accent, text, background) and a font, each with why; nothing is saved (brand.set with fromSite takes it)

cache.prefetch.description: Download everything the renders and reviews of a version or project need, for offline work (it carries on after a break, and checks each file)

cache.prune.description: Clear the copies on this machine that were used least recently (never ones kept for offline work or in use; MetaRush's storage is untouched)

cache.repair.description: Check every copy on this machine, remove damaged or half-downloaded ones, and download again the ones kept for offline work

cache.status.description: How much room this machine's copies of footage take: files, kept for offline work, in use, part-downloaded, and the size limit

captions.at.description: Which words a caption shows: the caption on screen at a frame of a version, the footage it comes from and what its transcript says there now

captions.check.description: Check a version's captions before it goes out: words the computer wasn't sure of, names not on the spelling lists, words fixed since the version

captions.file.description: A version's captions as a file (SubRip or WebVTT), with every text fix made since (no new render), or with the version's own words

captions.languages.description: The languages a project's captions are translated into, and how many of a version's lines each has (translated, fixed since, not yet)

captions.lines.description: A version's caption lines to translate into a language, with what is translated already and the spelling list as the glossary (Claude Code translates them on your own plan)

captions.looks.description: List the caption looks a cut can use (clean, the spoken word lighting up, boxed, big and bold, a box following the spoken word, plain subtitles): what each looks like and suits, and the house style's

captions.translate.description: Keep a translation of a version's caption lines into a language (Claude Code's, marked as machine-translated, or a person's); delivery writes a captions file per language

captions.translation.remove.description: Take a language's translated captions off a project (the captions in the original language stay)

catalogue.list.description: List what MetaRush can do as abilities, built in and added to this workspace, group by group: each says whether it works on this computer now or what it needs first (a key, a Mac, a program, an owner's approval)

catalogue.show.description: Show one ability of the menu, built in or added: what it does, the operation that runs it and the fields it fixes, what it needs, whether it works here, and the name a receipt records

collection.add.description: Put clips on a collection (with create, make the collection first when there is none by that name); they leave the Inbox and stay in their projects

collection.create.description: Create a collection: a named shelf for footage (B-roll, Family, Stock…) that projects can use

collection.delete.description: Delete a collection (never its clips: a clip on nothing else goes back to the Inbox; clips a project's cut uses through it are added to that project)

collection.list.description: List collections with how many clips each has and the projects that use them

collection.remove.description: Take clips off a collection (nothing is deleted; a clip on nothing else goes back to the Inbox); refused while a project's latest cut uses a clip through a link to it

collection.show.description: Show a collection: its clips (where else each one is) and the projects that use it

comment.add.description: Add a review comment (optionally pinned to a time)

comment.list.description: List review comments for a project or revision

components.add.description: Add an optional component to this computer (FFmpeg, the Remotion renderer, transcription…) with Homebrew or MetaRush's own checked download — people only

components.list.description: List MetaRush's components on this computer: what each unlocks, whether it is here, its size and how it is added

components.remove.description: Remove an optional component MetaRush added to this computer, and stop it being set up by itself — people only

consent.list.description: List consent records for making people's likeness in generated video

consent.record.description: Record consent to make a person's likeness: your own statement, or their recorded consent with what it covers and until when (people only; never a child or a public figure)

consent.revoke.description: Withdraw a consent: nothing new is made with that likeness, and looks that rely on it are withdrawn (people only)

content.follow.description: Make a project use another project's Content Settings (live: later changes there show up here; chains are followed, circles refused), or the default's

content.gate.set.description: Owners: say for a project's own Content Settings whether its videos wait for the quality check and sign-offs (on), only remind (off; people only) or follow the workspace

content.leave.description: Show what of a project may leave this computer, and to whom (the What may leave part of its Content Settings): footage, voices, faces, words and pictures, to AI services, abilities, Claude, cloud storage and delivery

content.leave.set.description: Change what of the projects using a project's own Content Settings may leave this computer, and to whom (people only: anyone may keep more here; letting more leave takes an owner)

content.logo.remove.description: Take one of the brand's named logos out of a project's own Content Settings (without a project, the default's); the picture stays in the resources and saved versions keep it

content.logo.set.description: Make a picture one of the brand's named logos in a project's own Content Settings (without a project, the default's): main, for dark backgrounds, for light backgrounds, a square icon or the wordmark; every project using the settings gets it, and graphics showing the main logo show the one made for their background

content.own.description: Give a project its own Content Settings: empty (or the ones it had before), or with copy a copy of the settings it uses now

content.pack.accept.description: Make the proposed layout pack the pack of a project's Content Settings (people only; every motion graphic in it must be approved)

content.pack.apply.description: Make a project's latest cut follow the layout pack of the Content Settings it uses (a checked change: graphics that name a part drawn with the pack's, call layouts in its look)

content.pack.decline.description: Set the proposed layout pack of a project's Content Settings aside (the pack stays as it was)

content.pack.preview.description: Previews of a project's layout pack in its brand and house style: each graphic on its own as the dashboard plays it (a motion graphic as its check's stills) and where call layouts place the pictures

content.pack.propose.description: Propose a whole layout pack for a project's Content Settings (its graphics may be project motion graphics): a draft that becomes the pack only when a person accepts it

content.pack.set.description: Change the layout pack of a project's own Content Settings (without a project, the default's): the template that draws a part and its choices, the pack's name, call layouts' looks, parts taken out, a shared library's newer version, or back to MetaRush's own; the latest cuts that don't follow it are offered

content.pack.show.description: The layout pack of a project's Content Settings (without a project, the default's): which template or approved motion graphic draws each title card, lower third, end screen, quote card and chapter card, how call layouts look, and a proposed pack waiting for a person

content.rules.add.description: Add a house rule (The name bar never animates) to a project's own Content Settings — every project using them follows it; without a project, the default's

content.rules.list.description: House rules: rules for every video using a project's Content Settings (a project's own rules stay in project.rules)

content.rules.remove.description: Take a house rule out of a project's own Content Settings (without a project, the default's)

content.setDefault.description: Use a project's Content Settings for new projects (its "Use for new projects"; there is one default, so this moves it): projects that use the default and footage in no project use them too

content.show.description: Show a project's Content Settings — its brand, spelling list, narration voice and house rules: whether they are its own, another project's (followed live) or the default's, and which projects use them too

content.signoffs.add.description: Add a house sign-off (Legal OKs it before export) to a project's own Content Settings — every project using them needs it; without a project, the default's

content.signoffs.list.description: House sign-offs: OKs every project using a project's Content Settings needs before a video goes out (a project's own sign-offs are cut.signoffs)

content.signoffs.remove.description: Take a house sign-off out of a project's own Content Settings (without a project, the default's)

content.style.apply.description: Make a project's latest cut follow the house style of the Content Settings it uses (a checked change: captions, name bar, name titles, framing, sound at cuts, the intro and end card when it has none)

content.style.set.description: Change the house style of a project's own Content Settings (without a project, the default's): captions, the name bar (look, height, animation), name titles, framing, sound at cuts, the intro and end card; new cuts start with it, and the latest cuts that don't follow it are offered

content.style.show.description: The house style of a project's Content Settings (without a project, the default's): what new cuts start with — captions, the name bar, name titles, framing, sound at cuts, an intro and an end card

conversation.angle.description: Change what a conversation clip shows from a moment on: one person, a layout (side by side, stacked, picture in picture, grid), a text card or a cutaway to other footage (checks the plan; apply makes it a new version)

conversation.cleanup.description: Look a conversation over for what calls leave behind: frozen webcams, sound dropouts, long silences, call talk ("can you hear me?", "you're on mute") and the app's chrome on a picture; each is a suggestion to accept or skip

conversation.create.description: Make a conversation from several recordings of one talk (one per person, or per-person sound and a shared gallery view): lines them up by their sound on one clock, with clock drift, and says how sure it is

conversation.cut.description: Make a cut of a conversation automatically: whoever is talking, switches in pauses (the voice leading the picture), listening reactions and the split layout when people talk together, in a style (podcast, off-camera interviewer, panel, reaction-heavy, talking head and b-roll), each choice with its reason (checks the plan; apply makes it a new version)

conversation.decide.description: Accept or skip clean-up suggestions: accepting cuts the stretch out of the cut, shows someone else over a frozen picture or crops the app's chrome off (checks the plan; apply makes it a new version)

conversation.detect.description: Say whether a set of files (names, as in a folder) is an online call: which app made it, who is in it, which file is whose sound or picture and whether they start together; the Add box offers "Make a conversation from these" with it

conversation.import.description: Bring in a call app's recording folder (Zoom with separate audio per participant, Riverside, SquadCast or any folder of per-person recordings) as footage and make a conversation of it, lined up as the app recorded it

conversation.list.description: List the conversations (in a project, or all of them) with their people, length and how sure their sync is

conversation.match.description: Match the webcams of a conversation: measure each person's picture where their face is and fit a colour and brightness correction to the reference, measured before and after (checks the change to the cut; apply makes it a new version)

conversation.moments.description: Find a conversation's best moments for shorts: complete stretches that start cleanly, each with why it might work (a question and its answer, laughing together, a strong first line); Claude chooses with the person

conversation.nudge.description: Move one recording of a conversation earlier or later on its clock, by seconds or frames (when lips and voice don't quite match)

conversation.pin.description: Use a conversation's current alignment and member settings in a project's cut (checks the change; apply makes it a new version)

conversation.settings.description: Change how a cut plays a conversation: each person's microphone quieter while they aren't speaking (and by how much), name tags in layouts, and a person's crop (checks the plan; apply makes it a new version)

conversation.short.description: Make a short from a stretch of a conversation: a new project with its own cut (vertical by default, captions with names, the picture following who talks) or the episode's stretch nested as it is

conversation.show.description: Show a conversation: its recordings, where each starts on its clock, how each was lined up and how sure, clean-up suggestions and the cuts that play it

conversation.styles.description: List the styles an automatic conversation cut can have and the layouts it can use

conversation.sync.description: Line a conversation's recordings up again: by their sound (default), as files that start together, on a clap in the first minute, or on moments a person marked in each

conversation.update.description: Rename a conversation, or change a member: their name, name tag, what their recording gives (picture and sound, sound only, picture only) and who they are in People

cut.add.description: Put footage into the latest cut as a new clip (all of it, or from a time or words to another), at the end, the start or next to a clip; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.apply.description: Save a checked cut sheet as a new revision (same confirm token and lock rules as edit.apply)

cut.captions.description: Choose how the latest version's captions look: one of the vetted looks, their size and place, the words per line, on or off; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.check.description: Check an edited cut sheet: problems by line, the changes in plain words, and a confirm token

cut.compare.description: Compare two revisions as cut sheets: the changes in plain words and the lines that differ

cut.copyIn.description: Copy another project's cut into this cut as a starting point: its clips, transitions, graphics, sound and narration (no live link; its footage becomes usable here)

cut.delete.description: Remove clips from the latest cut (by name or number); the rest closes up; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.deleteRange.description: Remove a stretch of the latest cut's timeline (from one time in the video to another, across clips); the rest closes up; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.diff.description: Compare an edited cut sheet with the revision it came from and with the latest revision

cut.flashes.description: Trim the split-second flashes of another picture at the edges of the latest cut's clips, at the exact switch, keeping the words; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.framing.description: Choose how the latest version frames its crops, for the whole cut or one clip: follow the subject as it moves, keep faces in frame, or keep the middle; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.move.description: Move a clip of the latest cut to the start, the end, next to another clip or to a place number; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.names.description: Cover the names a call app printed in the picture with the built-in name bar for the whole video, its name following who is on screen; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.nest.description: Put another project's cut into this cut as one clip, pinned to one version (it plays as that cut does: picture, sound, narration, graphics)

cut.pauses.description: Shorten long pauses between words in the latest cut (longer than one length, down to another), anywhere a clip has words; a dry run lists them to hear first, saving takes all or those picked (pick) with a confirm token

cut.removeWords.description: Take words out of the latest cut, cutting in the pauses around them: quoted words, a selection of a clip's words, or suggested ums, repeats and false starts (cleanup); dryRun checks it (and lists suggestions) with a confirm token

cut.rename.description: Name a project's cut descriptively (“Main open day video”), or take MetaRush's suggestion; no new version is saved and approvals stay

cut.say.estimate.description: Price changing a word or short phrase someone said into new words in their own voice copy, and check it may be made: whose voice (named by a person), their voice copy and the consent that covers new words with its service, the cut that plays it; nothing is sent or spent

cut.say.list.description: List words changed in a speaker's own voice copy, for a project or a clip: what was said and what is said now, whose voice, how it was checked, and whether the cut plays it

cut.say.make.description: Make new words in a speaker's own voice copy, with their consent, to replace a word or short phrase they said: priced first (maxUsd), people only, never automatic; the new words are checked by the recognizer and the voice's fingerprint before anyone can put them in the cut

cut.say.mouth.description: Match the mouth to new words made in a speaker's own voice copy (lip sync over the stretch, only when asked): every face there named by a person and consenting to lip sync with the service; priced first, people only; a dry run prices it

cut.say.place.description: Put new words someone said in their own voice copy (made and checked with cut say make) into the cut as a new version, with a review copy; people only; checked first like every edit (a dry run gives a confirm token)

cut.say.show.description: Show one word change made in a speaker's own voice copy: the words before and after, whose voice and consent, the price, how it was fitted and checked, and the versions that play it

cut.say.undo.description: Take changed words out of a cut again: a new version plays what was said (the change is kept, so it can be put back)

cut.show.description: Show a revision as a cut sheet (Markdown), the friendly editable form of the cut

cut.signoffs.add.description: Add a sign-off a cut needs before it goes out (Lena OKs the final version); a reminder before approving, exporting and delivering, and a hold on delivery while the ship gate is on

cut.signoffs.done.description: Tick a sign-off: that OK was given (for the cut's latest version; a house sign-off is ticked for this project only)

cut.signoffs.list.description: A cut's sign-offs: the OKs it needs before it goes out (the project's own and the house sign-offs of its Content Settings), and who gave them

cut.signoffs.remove.description: Take a sign-off off a cut's checklist (a house sign-off is taken out of its Content Settings instead: content.signoffs.remove)

cut.signoffs.undo.description: Untick a sign-off: the OK is needed again

cut.split.description: Cut a clip of the latest cut in two, at a time on the video's timeline or at a time or words in a clip's footage; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.transition.description: Change one cut of the latest version: the picture transition (dissolve, slide left…), the sound (split edits: lead, carry, auto) or a clip's fade-out; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.trim.description: Change where a clip of the latest cut starts or ends in its footage (a time, a change like +0.5 or quoted words), roll the cut with its neighbour, or slide its footage; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.update.description: Update the latest cut's resources and nested cuts to their newest versions (an explicit change, shown before it is saved)

cut.useFixed.description: Save a new version of a cut that plays a source's fixed copy (the steadier picture, the cleaned-up voices, the trimmed music, the fixed picture), or its original again; saved versions never change. dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token

cut.where.description: List the cuts that play this project's cut inside them (nested cuts)

database.abandon.description: Abandon a move of the database that stopped: changes go on in the old database, and the copy keeps its lock so nothing uses it (owners, people only)

database.move.description: Move the workspace's database to another one: changes pause on every computer, everything is copied and checked, this computer switches, and the old database is kept, marked as moved, never deleted (owners, people only; plan first)

database.move.status.description: Say which database this computer uses and whether the workspace is being moved to another one or moved (then switch this computer too), and how the last move started on this computer is going

database.plan.description: Check what moving the workspace's database would do — to the database on this computer, or to another MongoDB (Atlas or your own server) whose address this computer keeps for the move: what moves, how long it takes, what each computer needs, what waits meanwhile, and whether the new database is empty, reachable and writable; nothing is changed (owners)

database.switch.description: Switch this computer to the database the workspace moved to, with this computer's own sign-in for it (owners, people only, at this computer)

deliver.captions.description: Update the captions files of delivered videos with the text fixes made since (no new render; captions drawn into the video need a new version)

deliver.export.description: Copy finished renders of revisions to a local folder with descriptive names and a JSON sidecar each (hash-verified, never overwrites, never uploads)

delivery.gate.description: Whether versions wait for the quality check and their sign-offs before they go out: the workspace's choice and what a project's Content Settings say

delivery.gate.set.description: Owners: make versions wait for the quality check and their sign-offs before they go out (on), or only remind (off; people only)

delivery.notes.description: A version's delivery notes: its title (and other titles), description, chapters and show notes, as delivery writes them

delivery.notes.set.description: Save a version's delivery notes — title, other titles, description, chapters, show notes — written by Claude Code on your own plan or by a person; delivery writes them next to the video. The version itself never changes

delivery.override.description: Send a version out anyway past what holds it (the quality check, sign-offs), with a note: people only; the note is kept with who and when, and shows on the receipt and in what delivery writes. Never the approval

delivery.ready.description: Whether a version can go out to a client: Ready to deliver, or what holds it (the quality check's problems, a check that is missing or out of date, sign-offs still waiting, the approval, a render) with a one-step way to clear each, and the promises made to the client as measured

draft.decide.description: Decide about an AI app's draft — people only: approve (a version goes into the cut, a change is made), Not quite with what should change, or turn it down

draft.list.description: Drafts AI apps proposed, newest first: what each changes, its state (waiting, approved, Not quite with a person's note, turned down) and the decision

draft.save.description: Propose a change for a person to review, without making it: a new version of a cut (a cut sheet, an edit plan, a cut verb) saved as a draft outside the cut, or another change (Content Settings, names, notes) kept until a person approves it

edit.apply.description: Apply a checked plan, creating a new immutable revision (optimistic concurrency on the branch head)

edit.check.description: Dry-run a plan: schema + preflight validation, diff against the base, and a confirm token

edit.preview.description: Preview a plan without saving it: the cut it makes (rebased onto a newer version as saving would), its render plan for the player, problems in plain words, and a conflict when a newer version changes the same parts

edit.templates.description: List the vetted motion-graphics templates and their parameter schemas

edit.transitions.description: List the transitions (picture and sound) with plain descriptions, directions, easings, durations and the per-project styles

export.timeline.description: Write a version of a cut as a timeline for DaVinci Resolve (OpenTimelineIO), Final Cut Pro (FCPXML) or Premiere Pro (Final Cut Pro 7 XML), optionally with the original footage under readable names

extension.pair.description: Make a one-time code (10 minutes) that pairs your browser's MetaRush extension with this machine: what it sends is yours; it can only send videos and pages, never read anything; people only

extension.revoke.description: Unpair a browser's MetaRush extension: one of yours, all of yours, or (owners) anyone's; its token stops working at once

extension.status.description: The "Send to MetaRush" browser extension on this machine: its folder (for Load unpacked), your paired browsers (owners: everyone's), whether your pairing code is waiting

footage.analyze.description: Schedule local analysis (transcript, technical evidence, and what's on screen on a Mac) for an asset or a whole project

footage.captions.description: List the captions files kept with a clip (English captions an ability made for a clip in another language, for instance), or give one language's file

footage.describe.description: Have this machine's Claude Code write a sentence or two per scene of a clip (searchable; uses your Claude Code usage; on per project or workspace), or save descriptions Claude wrote in a session

footage.describe.configure.description: Turn written scene descriptions on or off for the workspace or one project (they use your Claude Code usage)

footage.describe.settings.description: Show whether written scene descriptions are on (workspace and project) and whether Claude Code can write them here

footage.evidence.description: Read technical evidence for an asset: scenes, pauses, black/frozen frames, loudness

footage.faces.description: List the faces seen in a clip: when each shows, where, and whose it is (named by a person, or recognized by the face and not confirmed yet)

footage.faces.name.description: Say whose face it is in that clip (confirming a face also teaches MetaRush what they look like, to recognize them in other clips)

footage.faces.notHere.description: Say a person appears nowhere on screen in a clip: never suggested for its faces (also faces found later), names given by looks go, and their voice is no evidence there

footage.faces.reject.description: Say a face is not someone (its name goes, and that person is not suggested for it again)

footage.frames.description: Extract still frames at given times to local JPEGs so Claude can look at them

footage.keyframes.description: Choose the frames of a contact sheet (one per shot, visual changes, new speakers, coverage) with their labels, without making the image

footage.language.description: Say which language a clip is spoken in, how MetaRush knows (heard, set by a person, or the workspace's) and what wrote its words down

footage.language.set.description: Set the language a clip is spoken in and write its words down again in that language (English with the English recognizer, other languages with whisper.cpp)

footage.moments.description: List grounded, timestamped candidate moments (speech, pauses, scene changes) across a project

footage.sheet.description: Build a labeled contact sheet (whole asset or a time range) as a local image: smart (one frame per shot, visual changes, new speakers, coverage) or even

footage.short.description: Make a short from any footage: one or more stretches (footage.moments lists moments) as a new cut for phones (tall), framed as the house style says unless a framing is asked for, captions on; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token; a person approves it like any cut

footage.speakers.description: List the voices in a video: names, how long each speaks, listening samples, suggestions, and notes about the people

footage.speakers.assign.description: Say who really says a stretch of a video (fix who said a line): the words move to that person, lines split where the speaker changes, and the voices learn only from what you confirmed

footage.speakers.detect.description: Find who speaks in videos (again): listens for the voices in the given videos, or in every video with a transcript but no voices yet

footage.speakers.hint.description: Say how many people speak in a video and find the voices again (keeps the words and the names people confirmed)

footage.speakers.reject.description: Say a voice is not a particular person (removes the suggestion or label, and that person's voice no longer learns from it)

footage.speakers.rename.description: Name a voice in a video; the same person is then recognized in other videos

footage.speakers.samples.description: Write each voice's listening samples to local WAV files

footage.speakers.unmerge.description: Separate two voices that were combined into one (undo giving them the same name)

footage.switches.description: Where a clip's picture switches (to the frame), who is on screen in each shot, and the names a call app printed in the picture

footage.switches.find.description: Find where a clip's picture switches, to the frame (a few seconds of work on any computer; again when asked)

footage.transcript.description: Read an asset's timed transcript (source seconds)

footage.visuals.description: Read what's on screen in a clip, in plain lines (shot type, faces and whose, setting, things, on-screen text), from the on-device index

footage.visuals.status.description: Say whether clips get looked at (Apple Vision on a Mac), on this machine and in the workspace, and how many are done

generate.again.description: Make new takes of a generated shot, made the same way (Generate again, Variations); never replaces a clip

generate.cancel.description: Stop a generated video that is waiting or being made

generate.configure.description: Change the generative-video model, draft and final quality, the daily limit or a project's budget (people only)

generate.edit.description: Change a clip by an instruction with generative video (make it night); a new clip, priced first

generate.estimate.description: Price a generated shot and check it may be made (consent, budget, this machine's key); nothing is sent or spent

generate.extend.description: Continue a clip (generated or your footage) with generative video; a new clip, priced first

generate.list.description: List generated videos (a project's, a look's, or a clip's takes) with what they cost

generate.settings.description: Show the generative-video settings: models and prices, draft and final quality, the daily limit and a project's budget

generate.shot.description: Make a new shot with generative video (Google Gemini) from a prompt, a look, a frame to start from or two frames, and pictures; priced first: needs maxUsd, the agreed estimate, unless your estimates are off

generate.show.description: Show how a generated video was made: prompt, look, pictures, settings, cost, safety, lineage and where it is used

improve.add.description: Put one idea on MetaRush's improvement list: something it couldn't do that the person needed (the same title again is the same idea)

improve.dismiss.description: Dismiss improvement ideas (not worth building); a later report finding them again leaves them dismissed

improve.export.description: Export improvement ideas as a Markdown document (kept and new by default)

improve.list.description: List improvement ideas found in the log (best first) and the reports they came from

improve.report.description: Make an improvement report now: signals from the log, read by Claude Code headless with the metarush-improve skill (no shell), saved as improvement ideas

improve.save.description: Save an improvement report (Markdown: one ## section per item with kind, impact, frequency and evidence lines) as improvement items

improve.schedule.description: Show the weekly improvement report's schedule on this machine (off unless turned on)

improve.schedule.set.description: Turn the weekly improvement report on or off on this machine, or change its day, hour or spending limit; people only, owners

improve.show.description: Show an improvement idea with its evidence, or a saved report

improve.signals.description: Find signals in the activity log: errors, retries, refused or ignored changes, corrections, Claude saying MetaRush cannot do something, long tool chains, slow operations

ingest.files.description: Ingest local files/folders: probe, hash, dedupe, upload (resumable), verify, then process

ingest.reconcile.description: Clean up abandoned uploads and stale ingest sessions (never touches available media)

ingest.sessions.description: List ingest sessions (uploads in progress, interrupted or finished)

ingest.url.description: Import videos from links (YouTube, TikTok, X): looked up, downloaded on this machine, then added like dropped files (dedupe, preview, transcript, speakers), with the original post recorded on the clip

ingest.url.configure.description: Change link-import settings on this machine: automatic weekly downloader updates, forget the remembered browser; owners

ingest.url.tools.description: Check the downloader link imports use on this machine: yt-dlp version and age, how it updates, its JavaScript runtime for YouTube, PO-token plugins

ingest.url.update.description: Update the downloader (yt-dlp) the way it was installed: brew upgrade, or yt-dlp -U for the self-contained build; owners

job.expedite.description: Process queued jobs now: heavy jobs may run on a machine that defers them for battery, and retry backoff is skipped

job.retry.description: Re-queue a failed or canceled job

job.show.description: Show one job in plain words: what it is, who started it, where it ran, why it waits, what it produced, and related project/clip/version/render/QA report

keep.add.description: Keep something a conversation brought in: a source, a logo and the brand kit, the brief, a rule or a check, a person's note, a sign-off, an idea for MetaRush, a spelling; it is never offered again

keep.decline.description: Decline something a conversation offered to keep: it is never offered again in the project

keep.list.description: What a project's conversations offered to keep: asked, kept and declined

library.list.description: The Library: the Inbox, collections, the Archive, footage in projects and the Trash, with counts; a search covers every view

log.configure.description: Change the log settings in config.yaml: where Claude conversation text is kept (workspace, local, off) and how many days entries stay (0 = until you delete them); owners

log.export.description: Export log entries (newest first) with their full texts, for a bug report or analysis

log.hooks.disable.description: Stop recording Claude Code terminal sessions: removes MetaRush's hooks (and nothing else) from Claude Code's settings; people only, owners

log.hooks.enable.description: Record Claude Code terminal sessions that use MetaRush: adds hooks to this machine's Claude Code settings; people only, owners

log.hooks.status.description: Check whether this machine's Claude Code records MetaRush terminal sessions into the log (opt-in hooks)

log.list.description: Read the activity log (newest first): operations, jobs, program runs, Claude turns and decisions, with filters

log.purge.description: Delete log entries older than a date (and the texts only they used); people only, owners

log.search.description: Search the activity log for words (summaries, errors, prompts and replies), newest first

log.settings.description: Show the log settings on this machine: where Claude conversation text is kept, how long entries stay, the Claude Code recording, what waits to be saved

log.show.description: Show one log entry in full: the prompt and reply of a Claude turn, a failed program's error output, and what belongs to it

looks.approve.description: Approve a look so new shots can use it (people only)

looks.create.description: Make a look for a person (with their consent) or a fictional character from stills and short clips (people only)

looks.list.description: List looks: how people and characters appear in generated video

looks.revoke.description: Withdraw a look: nothing new is made with it (people only)

looks.show.description: Show a look: its stills and clips, description, consent and test shots

looks.test.description: Make a look's test sheet: a few short draft shots to check it before approving (people only; priced first)

looks.update.description: Change a look; a change to what it shows needs approving again (people only)

machine.handover.abandon.description: Abandon a handover that hasn't been received: its conversations go on on the old computer (owners, people only)

machine.handover.clean.description: On the old computer, after the new one received its role: remove this computer's copies of the handed-over conversations (owners, people only, in a terminal; says what it would remove unless yes)

machine.handover.export.description: Make the handover file on the old computer: the panel conversations with their Claude Code sessions and folders, the pinned-work list and the folder settings, encrypted with a passphrase given at the terminal (owners, people only, in a terminal)

machine.handover.plan.description: Say what handing this computer's role to another computer would do: its panel conversations and whether each session is here, recipe runs and planning by itself, pinned work, watched and linked folders, remote access, extension pairings, which keys are here (names only), the background role, and the steps only a person takes (owners, people only; nothing changes)

machine.handover.receive.description: Receive a handover file on the new computer: sessions put where Claude Code looks, conversations held here from now on, pinned work moved, folders set where the person says (owners, people only, in a terminal; plan first)

machine.handover.status.description: Where this computer stands — the host, stepping down or a client since it handed its role over — and the handovers in progress (people only)

machine.invite.description: Mint a per-machine storage key (and optionally a database user) and write a 0600 join bundle; owners

machine.list.description: List the workspace's machines, their storage key labels (no secrets), state and last seen

machine.rekey.description: Give this machine a storage key of its own in place of the one it shares (minted, tested, switched; the old key is never deleted) — people only, owners

machine.rekeyPlan.description: Say what machine.rekey would do on this machine: its key, the machines sharing it, the new key's scope (changes nothing)

machine.revoke.description: Delete a machine's storage key (and optionally its database user) and mark it revoked; owners

machine.takeover.description: Take over the role of a computer that is gone: only when it hasn't been seen for a while and a person confirms it is off; its conversations from a plain copy of its folders or a handover file, its pinned work and folders move here (owners, people only, in a terminal; plan first)

mix.preview.description: Hear a sound mix change before saving it: the plan the preview plays with the change, and the mix in plain words (nothing is saved)

mix.set.description: Change a cut's sound mix: levels, mute and solo of the clips' sound, narration, music and effects, single clips' sound, ducking, loudness, speech leveling and cut blends (checks the plan; apply makes it a new version)

mix.show.description: Show a cut's sound mix in plain words: levels of the clips' sound, narration, music and effects, what is muted, ducking and loudness

motion.approve.description: Approve (or turn down) one exact version of a motion graphic after reviewing it — people only

motion.check.description: Check a project motion graphic: canonical archive and hash, import scan, type check, bundle, test frames and a preview in a network-jailed browser; a passing version is recorded for a person to approve

motion.list.description: List the project motion graphics checked in this workspace (latest version of each name, or every version), with their approval state

motion.new.description: Start a project motion graphic: motion/<name>/index.tsx (component, zod schema, meta) and preview.json

motion.revoke.description: Withdraw approval of a motion graphic version: new renders and checks of cuts that use it are refused — people only

motion.show.description: Show one motion graphic version: its source (with changes since the last approved version), imports, parameters, test frames, preview, decisions and the cuts that use it

notification.list.description: List your notifications (newest first) with the unread count

notification.read.description: Mark notifications read (by ID, or all)

ops.describe.description: Say how to use one operation (or another catalogue's entry): what it does, its input with an example, what it returns, its command and whether it changes anything or is people only

ops.find.description: Find what does a task, from words describing it: MetaRush's operations (and any catalogue that joins find), the best few first, one line each; nothing changes

people.compare.description: Compare two people's voices: how alike they sound and whether one is much lower

people.distinct.description: Say two people are different people (they are never asked about as the same person again)

people.evidence.description: How often each kind of evidence behind the questions about people was right (who is talking, the looks, names shown or said, the voice), and which no longer suggest names

people.learned.description: Show what a person's voice and face are learned from (the clips a person confirmed), how alike each is to the others and to a voice or face in question, and which one seems to be someone else

people.list.description: List the people named in this workspace, how much they speak, a few samples, and notes about them

people.merge.description: Combine two people who are really the same person

people.rebuild.description: Rebuild a person's voice from the clips a person confirmed (or everyone's), then re-check automatic labels and same-person questions

people.rename.description: Rename a person everywhere they appear

people.show.description: Show a person: every video they speak in, notes about them, and anyone whose voice sounds alike

people.split.description: Say a person's voice in one video is really someone else

people.unlearn.description: Take back a voice or face a person's name was learned from (say who it really is, or that you're not sure): their voice and face are learned again at once

people.update.description: Change the notes about a person (who they are, how to name or title them, what to highlight or avoid)

presenter.approve.description: Approve a presenter after its test clips, so clips can be made with it (people only)

presenter.list.description: List people's own presenters — a person's double at an AI service that reads lines on camera — with whose they are, where each stands and what it needs next

presenter.make.description: Make a person's presenter at the service from a training take of them and their reading of its consent words, with their recorded consent naming that service — people only, priced first

presenter.optout.description: Say whether an AI service trains its models on what it is sent, and whether its training opt-out is recorded as set for the key on this computer

presenter.optout.set.description: Record that an AI service's training opt-out is set for the account whose key this computer uses (or take that back): needed before a person's presenter is made at a service that trains on what it is sent (people only)

presenter.retire.description: Retire a presenter: nothing more is made with it, it is deleted at the service, clips waiting are stopped, and the cuts using its clips are listed (people only)

presenter.show.description: Show a presenter: whose it is, the look and consent it relies on, its training take, its test clips, the clips it read and the cuts that use them

presenter.start.description: Begin a person's own presenter from their approved look at an AI service: asks the service for the words the person reads on camera for its consent check (people only)

presenter.stock.description: List an AI service's stock presenters with their licence — only those whose licence covers commercial use and client work are offered — and whether it covers ads

presenter.test.description: Make a test clip of a presenter not yet approved, reading a clip's sound — people only, priced first

preview.prepare.description: Make a revision's preview sources (proxies, audio) local so the dashboard preview plays without buffering; reports progress

project.checkout.description: Write a project's cut into a folder (cut.md, footage.md, .metarush/lock.json) for editing and git

project.create.description: Create a project with an optional creative brief

project.delete.description: Delete a project: it moves to Archived projects, where anyone can restore it, and leaves Home, the project lists and search (its footage stays in the Library); people only

project.leaves.description: What of a project left this computer, and where: every request to an AI service, what Claude and AI apps were shown, the places abilities' runs reached, deliveries to folders a sync service uploads and Recipes' files, and cloud storage holding its media — with what its What may leave rules kept here; says so when nothing left

project.link.description: Let a project use another project's things — by default everything: its footage, resources, approved motion graphics and cut (nothing is copied) — or a subset

project.links.description: List the projects a project uses (and the projects that use it)

project.pull.description: Update a project folder to the latest revision (refuses to overwrite local changes unless forced)

project.purge.description: Clear archived (deleted) projects out for good: their versions, renders, Claude Code conversations and what they kept go; their footage goes back to the Inbox (never deleted); refused while another project's cut plays one of their cuts; owners, people only

project.push.description: Save a project folder's cut.md as a new revision (same check, confirm token and lock rules as cut.apply)

project.receipt.description: A project's receipt: every request to an outside AI service (service, model, kind, what was sent, cost, deleted there or not, why), Claude Code's conversations and whose account answered, generated media, Auto's spending, and the cost of the video at cost, per version and project

project.restore.description: Bring a deleted (archived) project back to Home and the project lists, as it was

project.rules.add.description: Add a rule to a project (First names only on screen), or a check a problem should get in every quality check; the same words twice are one rule

project.rules.list.description: A project's rules: plainly worded style rules and checks Claude follows and the quality check measures where it can

project.rules.remove.description: Take a rule out of a project

project.show.description: Show a project: assets, revisions, renders and the current head

project.sofar.description: What happened in a project so far, newest first: versions, renders, earlier Claude Code conversations and what was decided on their cards, open cards and questions

project.status.description: Show a project folder's local changes and whether a newer revision exists

project.unlink.description: Stop using another project's things; whatever this project's cuts already use stays usable (and the answer says what)

project.update.description: Rename a project, edit its brief, or archive it (archiving deletes it: people only, like project.delete)

project.use.description: Use specific things of another project in this one (footage, resources, motion graphics or its cut), without linking all of it

provider.list.description: List integrations (API-key providers such as ElevenLabs) and whether this machine has a key

provider.remove.description: Remove this machine's API key for an integration; owners

provider.set.description: Save this machine's API key for an integration (keychain, or <home>/.env for env-mode installations); tested first unless skipTest; owners

provider.settings.description: Change the narration voice of a project's own Content Settings (without a project, the default's): the voice, model, voice settings, region and favourite voices; or a project's budget

provider.status.description: Show one integration: key status on this machine (masked), last test, plan usage, shared voice/model settings and a project's budget

provider.test.description: Check the stored key (or a candidate key, without saving it) with the provider

publish.connect.description: Sign in to a video platform with your own account, in your browser on this computer (people only); the lasting permission is kept in this computer's keychain under you. forget takes it back

publish.plan.description: What posting a version to a video platform would send — the final render, the title, description and chapters from its delivery notes, captions files, privacy, who it is posted as — and what holds it (approval, a final render, the ship gate, client rules, signing in); nothing is sent

publish.platforms.description: The video platforms MetaRush posts to (YouTube) and your own sign-in to each on this computer, with what a person does next

publish.send.description: Post an approved version to a video platform as you (people only, every time; never Claude, Auto or an AI app): exactly what publish.plan shows, recorded on the version and the receipt

publish.setup.description: Register MetaRush with a video platform on this computer with the owner's own client (YouTube: an OAuth client for a desktop app from their Google Cloud project), kept in the keychain; or forget it

qa.run.description: Queue QA of a finished render: decode it, check conformance, black/frozen frames, loudness, silence vs. dialogue and layout, and extract frames

qa.show.description: Show a render's QA report: findings with timecodes, basis and suggested edit-plan fixes, measurements, and contact sheet/frame images

recipe.again.description: Make a run's video again with changes (new inputs, another voice): a new version of the same cut, the plan saying what changed and what is reused — people only

recipe.archive.description: Archive a recipe (or restore it): it leaves the Recipes tab and can't run; its versions and runs stay — people only

recipe.check.description: Check a recipe version (or a document): its inputs and where they go, against the graphics' fields, the word settings and approvals, then a dry assembly with its own inputs and stills of each section

recipe.checkout.description: Write a recipe version as its sheet: the recipe in Markdown — inputs, sections, the pack, bindings, rules, hints and its cut as a cut sheet — to read, edit and keep in git; check it and save it as a draft afterwards

recipe.compare.description: Compare two runs of a recipe: changed inputs, notes, recipe versions, cost, and the cut-sheet difference of the versions they made

recipe.continue.description: Let a run that waits for a person go on (after a budget was raised or consent recorded), agreeing to spend more when it asks — people only

recipe.diff.description: Say what changed between two versions of a recipe, in plain words: what changes each run, its sections, rules, sign-offs and hints, and its title, the video, where runs go, sound, graphics and pictures

recipe.export.description: Export a version of a recipe to a file another workspace can bring in: its document and sheet, the pictures it pins, the footage its cut plays and the approved code it uses by hash (motion graphics, shared libraries, Remotion versions)

recipe.import.description: Bring in a recipe file another workspace exported: a draft — a new version of the recipe it shares its history with, else a new recipe — with its pictures, footage and code in one project here; its words are data and its code waits for a person's approval here

recipe.list.description: List the workspace's recipes: what each makes, its inputs, its example and its last runs (archived ones with archived)

recipe.picks.description: Keep or change a run's first picks: the moments MetaRush picked for its chosen sections (their clips in the run's cut) and the stretches of its pack's shorts, or drop one; the run goes on once every pick is kept or changed

recipe.plan.description: Plan a run of a recipe (nothing starts): the inputs as they will be, where the video goes, each step, one estimate in dollars that opens to each step's outside service, model, source and price, whether the person is asked to agree to it, and a fingerprint

recipe.propose.description: Show what saving a project's cut as a recipe would vary each run and keep (nothing is saved): the proposal, with the keys vary, keep, fixed and chosen take, the recipe in plain words and its check

recipe.publish.description: Make a version of a recipe current: the one runs make (removed rules are named) — people only

recipe.run.description: Start a run of a recipe a person agreed to (the plan's fingerprint and an amount at least its estimate): a new project or a new cut, made through the ordinary steps — people only

recipe.runs.description: List runs of recipes (when, who, where, cost, approved), or show one with its steps and what it waits for

recipe.sample.description: Approve a run's sample (the rest of the run is planned then and asks for its agreement) or say it isn't right (the run stops, with your note) — people only

recipe.save.description: Save a project's cut as a recipe: MetaRush proposes what varies (the project's own footage, words in graphics, word settings, pictures, the voice) and what stays; vary, keep, fixed and chosen move items; a person's save is current, Claude's a draft

recipe.show.description: Show a recipe: its versions, inputs (type, default and limits), sections, sound, rules, hints, its last check and its runs

recipe.starters.description: List the starter recipes MetaRush comes with (a call becomes an episode with shorts; a release tag becomes a release video): what each makes, what a run gives it, the abilities it uses, and whether this workspace has it

recipe.starters.add.description: Add MetaRush's starter recipes (all, or those named) to the workspace as drafts, with their example footage and pictures in the project “Starter recipes”; a person makes each current before it runs

recipe.stop.description: Stop a run: work it asked for that hasn't started is called off; what it made stays

recipe.suggestions.description: Suggest changes to a recipe from what people changed in its runs (each run's approved version against the one it made): a change that repeats — you shortened the intro in 4 of 5 runs — with plain reasons and what a draft would change; nothing is saved

recipe.suggestions.save.description: Save a recipe's suggested changes (from what people changed in its runs) as a draft version; only a person makes it current

recipe.triggers.description: Say when recipes plan a run by themselves (new footage or pictures where an input takes them from, a weekly time), whom they tell, which computer looks and the plan waiting; they never start a run

recipe.triggers.set.description: Turn planning by itself on or off for a recipe — when new files arrive where an input takes them from, or every week at a time — or set aside the plan it made; it tells you and never starts a run — people only

recipe.update.description: Make a draft version of a recipe from a version with changes (a merge patch over its document, a title, hints or rules to add); a person makes it current

recipe.write.description: Save a recipe sheet as a draft: a new version of the recipe it names (built on the version it was written from), or a new recipe; a person makes it current

recording.cut.description: Start a cut from a screen recording: the screen with the camera in a corner, side by side, the screen only or the camera only, the voice playing throughout (checks the plan; apply makes it a version)

recording.discard.description: Throw away a screen recording that isn't footage yet: the pieces that arrived are deleted (people only; footage already in the Library goes to the Trash there)

recording.finish.description: Make a screen recording footage: its voice, screen and camera become clips in the Library, lined up on its clock and linked into its project (keep: what arrived, after a closed tab or a lost connection)

recording.link.description: Link a screen recording into a project: its footage joins the project as one conversation (screen, camera and voice lined up), so a cut can lay them out together

recording.list.description: List the screen recordings made in the dashboard (in a project, or all of them): their tracks (screen, camera, voice), length, and whether they are footage yet

recording.show.description: Show a screen recording: each track (screen, camera, voice), where it starts on the recording's clock, the footage it became, the projects it is linked into and what is left to do

remote.allow.description: Add or remove Tailscale accounts that are signed in by themselves through remote access (adding only from this computer); people only, owners

remote.disable.description: Turn remote access off: the address and the Tailscale accounts are cleared and browsers on other computers are signed out; says how to stop tailscale serve; people only, owners

remote.enable.description: Set up remote access over Tailscale (this computer's Tailscale name as the address, who signs in with their Tailscale account) and say which tailscale serve command starts it; people only, owners

remote.signout.description: Sign out browsers that signed in from other computers (all, or one Tailscale account's); people only, owners

remote.status.description: Remote access over Tailscale: the address people use from their other computers, whether tailscale serve hands it to this dashboard, HTTPS certificates, and who signs in with their Tailscale account

remotion.allow.description: Allow the packages a version of a Remotion source adds or changes, so MetaRush may install them — people only

remotion.approve.description: Approve (or turn down) one version of a Remotion source after reviewing it, and move the latest cuts' clips to it — people only

remotion.check.description: Check an edited checkout as the next version (or check a recorded version again): the change in plain words, packages, a type check, the compositions it affects, and before/after stills drawn in the render jail; a passing version waits for a person

remotion.checkout.description: Write a version of a Remotion source into a folder to edit (MetaRush's branch, with git for diffs); check it afterwards to make the next version

remotion.import.description: Bring a Remotion project (a folder on this computer or a GitHub repository) into a project as a source: its files kept as the first version (secrets, installed packages and other tools' settings left out), its packages, fonts and compositions read in the render jail, and the videos it already had added as footage

remotion.lift.description: Turn a composition of a Remotion source, or one of its scenes, into a reusable motion graphic: its component becomes the graphic (its props the parameters) and the files it shares become the project's shared library (theme, components, words; its Google Fonts as font resources); both are checked with no network and wait for a person's approval

remotion.list.description: List the Remotion sources of a project (or every project): where each came from, its versions and approval, its compositions with size, frame rate and length, and the clips made from it

remotion.map.description: Show the project map of a Remotion source's version: each composition's scenes with their times and what sets their lengths, the words on screen with where they are written, pictures, sounds with their timing and level, fonts and timing data, and a still per scene (made in the render jail the first time)

remotion.pictures.description: Show the pictures a Remotion source draws: its settings (each picture with the one that replaces it, where the code names it and where it is seen), or what the one-time change would make settings, and the pictures its code works out as it plays

remotion.pictures.set.description: Replace pictures of a Remotion source whose pictures are settings, with pictures from the project's resources (or files on this computer, added to them): drawn in the render jail (lengths, whether the new picture shows, its shape, before/after stills), then the latest cuts' clips are made again with them — no new version of the code

remotion.pictures.setup.description: Make a Remotion source's pictures settings: the one-time change to its code (each picture it draws wrapped so it can be replaced) as the next version, checked in the render jail; a person approves it

remotion.push.list.description: List the changes sent back to a Remotion project's repository: versions, branches, pull requests

remotion.push.plan.description: Show what sending an approved version's changes back to the Remotion project's repository would do: the changes in plain words (files, words, packages), where they go, the new branch and the pull request

remotion.push.start.description: Send an approved version's changes back to the Remotion project's repository as a new branch, and a pull request on GitHub — people only; never forced, never the default branch

remotion.refresh.log.description: Read what a refresh's steps printed (keys and other secrets hidden)

remotion.refresh.plan.description: Show what a refresh of a Remotion source would do before anything runs: its own steps (npm scripts, its files, its tools) with their commands, the keys from Settings → Integrations passed and the names they get, where the steps may write, the hosts they may reach and how they are kept away from MetaRush's files

remotion.refresh.runs.description: List the refreshes of a Remotion source: their steps, how each went, what they changed and left out, and the version they made

remotion.refresh.start.description: Start a refresh a person looked at (people only): the source's own steps run on this computer, outside the render jail with the network on, in a separate environment that gets only the keys picked; what they write becomes a new version that waits for a person

remotion.render.description: Make a composition of an approved version into a clip: rendered in the render jail with the source's own packages (once per version, composition, props and frames) and added to Sources as footage

remotion.revoke.description: Withdraw approval of a version of a Remotion source: new renders and cuts that use its clips are refused — people only

remotion.show.description: Show one Remotion source and a version: its compositions, packages, settings, what the import left out, the check (the change in words, before/after stills), decisions and renders

remotion.stills.description: Draw frames of a composition of any version in the render jail (nothing is saved): pictures on this computer to look at

remotion.update.description: Move a project's latest cut to the newest approved version of a Remotion source: its clips are rendered again from that version and saved as a new version of the cut

remotion.use.description: Put a composition of an approved version into a project's cut: the clip it already has, or rendered first and added when it is done

remotion.words.description: Show a Remotion source's on-screen words: its settings (the words as the code writes them and as changed, where they are written and where they are seen), or the files that hold its words when they aren't settings yet

remotion.words.set.description: Change on-screen words of a Remotion source whose words are settings: drawn in the render jail with the new words (lengths, words that no longer fit, before/after stills), then the latest cuts' clips are made again with them — no new version of the code

remotion.words.setup.description: Make a Remotion source's on-screen words settings: the one-time change to its code (its copy files wrapped so words come from settings) as the next version, checked in the render jail; a person approves it

render.cancel.description: Cancel a queued or running render

render.fetch.description: Download a finished render to a local file (verified by SHA-256)

render.follow.set.description: Turn the review copy that follows each cut's latest version on (the default) or off

render.follow.show.description: Whether a review copy follows each cut's latest version (made by itself about a minute after the last change), and the copies it is making now

render.status.description: Show a render and its job progress

render.submit.description: Queue a render of a revision; returns the render and job (it is NOT done until state is available)

resources.add.description: Add pictures (PNG, JPEG, WebP; HEIC converted), SVGs (cleaned), PDFs (pages become pictures) and fonts to a project's resources or the workspace library; a folder is linked and kept in step

resources.fetch.description: Bring in a GitHub repository (pinned at a commit: its text files, README, languages and history; binaries and large files left out) or a web page (a dated snapshot: screenshots for a computer and a phone, the whole page, its text, title, colours and icon). It runs as a job on this machine

resources.folder.description: Change a linked folder: when files upload, pause or resume it on this machine, link it here at a path, or look through it again

resources.folders.description: List linked folders: where each is on this machine, and how it stands on every machine

resources.link.description: Link a folder on this machine: its pictures, SVGs, PDFs and fonts become resources (and its footage sources), kept in step as files change

resources.list.description: List the resources (pictures, logos, SVGs, PDFs, fonts) a project can use — its own, the workspace library's and its linked projects' — or the workspace library

resources.make.description: Make a code slide (a repository file's lines, highlighted), a diagram (Mermaid or D2, drawn as SVG) or a repository card, as a resource that says exactly where it came from

resources.path.description: Fetch a resource's file (or a PDF page picture) to this machine and return its path, so Claude can look at it

resources.pictures.description: List the pictures a GitHub repository keeps from its folders: each a picture of its own pinned to the commit, with what was left out and why

resources.pictures.set.description: Keep the pictures (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF, SVG) in a GitHub repository's folders as pictures of their own, pinned to the commit and refreshed with it, or stop keeping a folder in step; nothing from a repository ever runs

resources.promote.description: Move a project's resource into the workspace library, so every project can use it (cuts that use it don't change)

resources.refresh.description: Look at a resource again: size, colours, page pictures (after installing poppler) and suggested tags (the file never changes); a repository moves to its newest commit and a web page gets a new snapshot (new versions: cuts use them after cut update)

resources.remove.description: Remove a resource from the library (nothing is deleted: cuts that use it keep rendering it), or restore one
