resources.show.description: Show one resource: its versions, size, colours, tags, where it came from and where it is used

resources.unlink.description: Stop keeping a linked folder in step (on every machine, or only this one); its resources stay

resources.update.description: Rename a resource, change its short name, tags, description or licence note

resources.where.description: List where a resource is used: cuts (and their older versions) and the brand kit

review.packet.description: One page for a draft or a version, to hand to a client or a colleague: what changed and why, the checks, the cost, who made it and what is still waiting (format markdown: also as Markdown)

review.waiting.description: Awaiting your review: each cut's latest version when it is a draft an AI app (Claude, Codex, Cursor…) made or someone asked to have reviewed, and the drafts AI apps proposed — versions not in the cut yet and other changes (hand edits saved in the background don't wait)

revision.approve.description: Approve (or reject) a revision — people only

revision.askReview.description: Ask for review: the version waits in “Awaiting your review” for people to approve it or say what should change

revision.compare.description: Compare two revisions (clips, overlays, audio, captions, duration)

revision.note.description: Change a version's note: a few words saying what it changed (“flicker fixes and headline cards”); the version itself never changes

revision.plan.description: Resolve a revision into its frame-accurate render plan (proxy URLs for preview)

revision.show.description: Show a revision including its full spec

search.description: Search transcripts (what was said, with timecodes and who said it), what's on screen (things, animals, places and on-screen text the on-device index saw, and written scene descriptions, with time ranges), people's names (the videos they speak in), video titles/filenames, projects, revisions, comments and resources (logos, pictures, PDFs, fonts: name, tags, description); a project's search includes what its project links bring in; ranked exact phrase > all words > partial

setup.status.description: Say what works on this computer: free with no keys, what a key adds, Claude Code's sign-in and where the projects are kept

share.create.description: Send a version for review to someone outside the workspace: an expiring link to its review copy, its words if you allow, and comments pinned to times that come back as the version's comments (people only)

share.link.description: The link to send again for a review link that still works (people only)

share.list.description: Review links sent to people outside the workspace: a project's, a version's or all, with what each shows, until when, and the comments that came back

share.plan.description: What a review link to a version would show people outside the workspace, for how long, and whether it may be made (who may share, What may leave, the review copy, the media store)

share.revoke.description: Take a review link back: its page and its copy of the video are deleted at once, so it stops opening; its comment slots once their last comments are read; comments already in stay (people only)

share.settings.description: Who may send review links to people outside the workspace and for how long, and whether this workspace's media store can hold their pages

share.settings.set.description: Turn review links for people outside the workspace on or off, let only owners send them, or shorten the longest a link lasts (owners)

share.sync.description: Bring in new comments from review links now (the dashboard's computer does it every two minutes), and end links whose time is up

sound.compare.description: Compare voices before and after they were made clearer: the voice clarity score, the background noise and warnings when it went too far

sound.enhance.description: Make a voice clearer — a person over their speech, the narration, a recording or everyone — on this computer (clean, studio) or with ElevenLabs (cloud, priced first and budgeted); the recordings are kept, results are cached; estimate says what it takes (checks the plan; apply makes it a new version)

sound.levels.description: Change how loud things are: camera sound, narration, music, effects, single people over their speech, single clips, music getting quieter when someone talks, voices evened out, smooth cuts, overall loudness and each music track's level (checks the plan; apply makes it a new version)

sound.music.add.description: Put music under a cut: timed to the video by default (it starts with it and ends with it on a beat, with a smooth fade; a shorter track fades early or loops) or placed by hand; its level and whether it gets quieter when someone talks (checks the plan; apply makes it a new version)

sound.music.set.description: Change a music track: fit it to the video or time it by hand (in, out and where it starts), its level, getting quieter when someone talks, looping, or take it out (checks the plan; apply makes it a new version)

sound.preview.description: Hear a sound change before saving it — or every voice as recorded (A/B): the plan the preview plays and the mix in plain words (nothing is saved)

sound.setup.description: Set up clearer voices on this computer: the voice cleaner and the clarity score (clean, about 30 MB) or studio quality (about 1.8 GB) — people only

sound.show.description: Show a cut's sound in plain words: how loud each part and each person is, clearer voices (and how much they helped), the automatic help, music and the ways to make voices clearer on this computer

storage.migrate.description: Move this workspace's media to another storage (S3-compatible, Google Cloud Storage or a folder): copy every file resumably, each checked by SHA-256, then switch this machine and the workspace to it; the old storage is left as it was; owners

storage.plan.description: Check what moving this workspace's media to another storage would copy (a dry run: it lists both storages and changes nothing)

storage.status.description: Say which storage this machine uses and which one the workspace names (after another machine moved the media: this machine still uses the old storage, and the new one to switch to), whether a move runs here, and how the last move started from the dashboard on this machine went

sync.status.description: What is on this machine and what is only in MetaRush's storage, waiting imports and jobs, which machines run MetaRush, and whether the database and the storage answer

timeline.import.description: Make a new cut from a timeline exported from another editing app: its clips matched to the Library's footage, transitions, split edits, sound levels, chapters and notes, through the edit check; dryRun checks it and gives a confirm token; questions about footage not found are answered with answers (relink, add or skip)

timeline.read.description: Read a timeline exported from another editing app (OpenTimelineIO, FCPXML, Final Cut Pro 7 XML, EDL) and say what it would become: its clips, the footage found in the Library and questions for footage not found, chapters, and what can't be carried over; nothing is changed

todos.acceptShown.description: Accept the names a clip shows (a call app's name tiles, lower thirds) for the people it asks about: one answer per question

todos.answer.description: Answer a question; the answer is applied (names a voice, records music rights, fills the brief…)

todos.counts.description: Count open questions per video, project and kind (for badges)

todos.dismiss.description: Dismiss a question (it will not be asked again)

todos.groups.description: List the questions about faces: one per person per clip, with sample faces, how often they are seen, the suggested name and why (names the video shows or says, the voice, the looks)

todos.list.description: List open questions MetaRush needs a person to answer (filter by project, video or kind)

todos.notPerson.description: Say none of the open questions about faces that suggest a person are them (in a project, a clip, or everywhere): they're never suggested for those faces again

todos.show.description: Show one question with what to listen to or look at and how to answer

todos.skipFaces.description: Skip every open question about faces in a clip or a project: those faces are never asked about again (they can still be named by hand)

todos.sync.description: Re-check a project or video for questions that need a person (and close ones that no longer apply)

transcript.find.description: Find words in transcripts (one clip, a project or everywhere): every place with the words around it, to listen to before changing anything

transcript.fix.description: Retype what is said in a stretch of a clip's transcript (the words keep their timing; the machine's transcript is kept, and the fix can be undone)

transcript.history.description: A clip's transcript fixes, newest first: who changed what and when, which can still be undone, and the machine's own transcript

transcript.pending.description: Text fixes made since a version of a cut that touch its words: they wait for a new version (nothing renders by itself)

transcript.pending.apply.description: Make one new version of a cut with every text fix made since its latest version, and one review copy (instead of rendering after each fix)

transcript.replace.description: Change words wherever they are said in transcripts (one clip, a project or everywhere), or only the places you ticked; joined or split words keep their timing

transcript.speaker.description: Say who really says a stretch of a clip ("this part is Lena, not Maya"); recorded in the clip's transcript history so it can be undone

transcript.spelling.add.description: Put a word on the spelling list of a project's own Content Settings ("always write FernBrook"; without a project, the default's): new transcripts are corrected by it and the transcriber is told to expect it

transcript.spelling.apply.description: Correct existing transcripts by the spelling lists (one clip, a project, every clip using a project's settings, or everywhere); dryRun only lists the places

transcript.spelling.list.description: The spelling list a project uses — part of its Content Settings (its own, another project's or the default's): how names and terms are always written

transcript.spelling.remove.description: Take a word off the spelling list of a project's own Content Settings (without a project, the default's); transcripts it corrected stay as they are

transcript.spelling.suggestions.description: Words people keep fixing the same way that aren't on a spelling list yet

transcript.undo.description: Undo a transcript fix, or a whole find and replace (every place it changed)

trash.configure.description: Turn “Empty the Trash after N days” on (a person decides) or off (0); owners

trash.empty.description: Delete clips in the Trash for good (all of it, or the ones named), with their previews, transcripts and speaker data, on every machine; clips a cut uses stay; people only, owners

trash.list.description: List what is in the Trash: when each clip went there, from where, whether it can be deleted for good, and the total size

trash.settings.description: Whether the Trash empties itself after a number of days (off unless a person turns it on)

users.disable.description: Turn a person's account off: signed out everywhere, can't sign in (owners)

users.enable.description: Turn a person's account back on (owners)

users.invite.description: Invite a person by email: a one-time link they follow to choose a password (owners)

users.list.description: The workspace's people: accounts, invites, earlier people and their roles

users.remove.description: Remove a person's account; their name stays on what they did (owners)

users.resetLink.description: A one-time link a person follows to choose a new password (owners)

users.revoke.description: Take back a person's invite or reset link (owners)

users.role.description: Make a person an owner or a member (owners)

version.show.description: Show this computer's MetaRush version, what's new in it and the version each computer in the workspace runs

voiceover.addTake.description: Register part of an audio asset as a take for a narration line (used by the recorder)

voiceover.align.description: Match a transcribed recording to the script and place it (split at each line, or as one piece); measures the narrator's pace

voiceover.askFit.description: Ask your local Claude Code (read-only) to fit the script to the video: it proposes a version with lines tied to the right moments and trimmed to fit, every change explained; you review it line by line and the original is kept

voiceover.choose.description: Put a take — or the original or cleaned-up version of the current one — on a narration line (checks the plan)

voiceover.cleanup.description: Clean up recorded narration with a preset (noise, rumble, harsh s, level, leading silence) as a second version the line can switch to

voiceover.clone.description: Create an ElevenLabs voice from recordings of your own voice (anyone else's needs their recorded consent) — people only

voiceover.estimate.description: Price ElevenLabs narration before generating: characters and credits per line, free cached lines, budget and plan allowance

voiceover.fit.description: Check whether every narration line fits before the next one, and build the fix (extend the shot, speed up AI speech ≤ 8%, start earlier, move the next line)

voiceover.fitted.description: Use Claude's version of the script fitted to the video (the original is kept), or choose line by line which version to keep; shows both side by side and checks the plan

voiceover.line.description: Add, change, move or remove one narration line (words, delivery notes, its own voice, where it starts — tied to a shot, a moment, the previous line or a clock time — or its place in the script), and check the plan

voiceover.models.description: List the ElevenLabs models this account can use, with languages, text limits and cost per character

voiceover.parse.description: Turn a plain-text script into narration lines (paragraphs; [@clip+0.5], [0:12.4], [after], (notes)) and check the plan that sets it

voiceover.place.description: Put a live take (recorded while the video played) where it was spoken: each line gets its piece of the recording, cut only in pauses, and a start point where it was said; or put an earlier take back, each line where it was spoken or at its planned spot

voiceover.preview.description: Download a voice's sample to a local file (the dashboard streams samples instead)

voiceover.scratch.description: Make free scratch narration with a system voice (macOS say or espeak-ng) for timing review, and check the plan that adds it

voiceover.show.description: Show a cut's narration: each line, where it plays, whether it fits, its audio and takes

voiceover.takes.description: List the audio takes made or found for narration lines

voiceover.tts.description: Generate ElevenLabs narration with word timing (unchanged lines are reused for free; respects the project budget), and check the plan that adds it

voiceover.use.description: Switch the narration between your original script and Claude's fitted version (the other one is kept with its sound and places)

voiceover.voices.description: List voices: ElevenLabs (your account or the public library) or the free local scratch voices

watch.browse.description: List folders under your home folder (the watched-folder picker; never leaves the home folder)

watch.choose.description: Open the native folder picker on this machine (macOS) and return the chosen folder

watch.disable.description: Stop watching the folder (the folder setting is kept); owners

watch.import.description: Also add the files that were already in the watched folder when it was set to take only new files

watch.mkdir.description: Create a folder under your home folder (for the watched-folder picker); owners

watch.reveal.description: Open the watched folder (or another folder) in Finder

watch.set.description: Configure and enable the watched folder (writes only worker.watch in config.yaml; the running daemon picks it up without a restart); owners

watch.status.description: Show the watched folder: configuration, state (watching, off, missing), last scan, files waiting to settle, last ingest and errors

worker.configure.description: Change this installation's worker settings (heavy-job battery threshold) in its config.yaml; owners

worker.list.description: List workers, their capabilities, load and liveness

worker.settings.description: Show this installation's battery state and heavy-job battery policy

workspace.adopt.description: Say this restored copy is now the workspace: it deletes by itself again as set (the Trash on its schedule, review links ending, old activity cleared out), once the original is retired or the copy has storage of its own (owners, people only)

workspace.export.description: Export the whole workspace into one archive — projects, versions, transcripts, people and consent records, conversations, the log, and the footage when included — for a backup or a move (owners, people only; --plan first)

workspace.exports.description: List the exports of the workspace made on this computer and how far each one is (owners, people only)

workspace.show.description: Show the connected workspace, installations and storage
